state.context: CanLang is a compact AI-authored SaaS DSL with canonical CRUD/scenarios, generated forms, inline BDD, explicit grants and schema reuse. CRM requires CSV row validation and duplicate review. CSV export already exists but supplies no import behavior. Do not create a parallel write path or copied input schema. The attached source fixes actual customer-manager authority and limited directory visibility.
state.candidate: Candidate form contract: import=csv adds a reviewed multirow mode to an existing canonical mutation form. Optional review names an existing pure read scenario; its required named inputs are a type-compatible subset of the form operation inputs, including protected bound references. It returns an array of readable records, never grants extra fields. No copied schema or input scope is added. Each row remains editable/excludable. Server validates typed cells and grants, shows candidate matches, and requires explicit confirmation; it never merges or chooses a record by a display label. Missing/invalid cells cannot commit. Commit invokes canonical operation once per confirmed row in source order, with current authority and stable per-row operation identity. These are separate transactions, not all-or-nothing batch semantics. Completed rows stay completed, failure/pending/unknown is visible, retries reuse identities, edited previously committed rows require a new explicitly reviewed row. Recompute review before invoking each row; changed candidate sets require renewed confirmation rather than hidden duplicate creation. This catches candidates created by earlier rows too. Custom review does not replace business invariants or promise uniqueness. Typed reference IDs/versions and pinned money/date/array representations reuse existing operation schemas; bound identity/parent values cannot be overridden. CSV is transient UTF-8 input capped by shared limits, not an attachment granting file access. Parsing uses comma/header/quote rules from RFC4180, with explicitly allowed LF and optional UTF-8 BOM; CSV dialect guessing is excluded. The UI calls the same business operations available through MCP; upload/review-session mechanics are not a second CRUD API.
state.url_candidate: A second gap is absolute outbound links for the proposed /offers/respond/{Revision.id} response page using the existing record-route mechanism. The opaque record ID locates its team; verified recipient policy still authorizes it. Page routes have no authored names, strings can format relative paths, and deployment already has a canonical public origin. Consider app_url(path:text)->url as a closed pure builtin joining a relative app path to that trusted configured origin. Reject absolute/scheme-relative paths, credentials, backslashes and invalid encoded path forms; query/fragment are allowed as encoded path suffixes. Require a single initial slash and reject dot segments after decoding; never use a caller Host header. This grants no token/record authority and does not replace route guards. Deployment prefixes remain canonical configuration. No new named-route registry or app-authored domain string is required.

csv_form.instructions: Compare three ways of expressing reviewed CSV intake against token cost, schema ownership, permissions, agent readability and precise partial-failure behavior.

criteria.form: Extend the existing form with import=csv and optional review=readScenario. The owning operation supplies the input schema; review takes a named subset of those inputs and returns readable model candidates. Reuses ordinary controls but gives form metadata more responsibilities.
criteria.scenario: Add a typed batch scenario and standard CSV parser capability for each intake. It makes parsing and per-row effects explicit and permits custom orchestration, but repeats row schemas or needs operation-input type reflection and adds business wrapper operations.
criteria.automatic: Generate CSV review for every eligible mutation form, deriving candidates only from unique constraints and exact duplicate inputs. This needs no new authored form tokens, but cannot express CRMs nonunique email or case-folded-name candidate search without another extension.

csv_semantics.instructions: Does this candidate preserve canonical permissions/schema ownership and define review changes, partial outcomes and replay without silently promising atomic bulk import?

app_url.instructions: Is app_url with that narrow trusted-origin contract sufficient for absolute outbound app links without granting access or guessing a deployment URL?
